title: möchten and wollen
situation: Ordering and saying what you want
canDo: You can order politely with möchten and say what you and others want with wollen.
explanation:
In a café or restaurant you order with **möchten** (would like): *Ich möchte einen Kaffee, bitte.* With friends and family you often say what you want with **wollen**: *Was willst du heute machen?*

| | möchten | wollen |
|---|---|---|
| ich | **möchte** | **will** |
| du | möchtest | willst |
| er/sie/es | **möchte** | **will** |
| wir | möchten | wollen |
| ihr | möchtet | wollt |
| sie/Sie | möchten | wollen |

Like können and müssen, **ich** and **er/sie/es** have no ending: *er möchte, sie will.*

You can use them in two ways:
- with a noun (accusative): *Ich möchte **einen** Tee. Die Kinder wollen Pizza.*
- with a second verb at the **end**: *Wir möchten **bezahlen**. Er will nicht **warten**.*

**möchten** is polite: use it when you order or ask for something. **wollen** is more direct. *Ich will einen Kaffee!* to a waiter sounds rude.

The most common mistake: *ich will* does **not** mean "I will". It means "I want": *Ich will nach Hause gehen.* = I want to go home.

Useful: ***Wollen wir** Pizza essen?* = Shall we have pizza?
french: möchten is like « je voudrais » and wollen like « je veux », and just as in French, « je veux » sounds too direct when you order.

examples.de: Möchten Sie noch etwas? – Nein, danke.
examples.en: Would you like anything else? – No, thank you.

examples.de: Was willst du heute machen? – Ich will schwimmen gehen.
examples.en: What do you want to do today? – I want to go swimming.
Would you like a piece of cake?
The children want to eat pizza.

items.en: I'd like a coffee, please.
What would you like to drink?

items.why: er/sie/es takes the same form as ich, with no ending: er möchte.
items.en: He'd like a beer.
I'd like to pay.
We'd like to order.

items.why: wollen changes its vowel in the singular: du willst.
items.en: What do you want to do today?
The children want to eat pizza.

items.why: Formal Sie takes the same form as wir: Möchten Sie …?
items.en: Would you like anything else?
He doesn't want to wait.
Would you like a piece of cake?
What do you want to eat?
What would you like to order?

items.why: The second verb goes to the end in the infinitive.
items.en: I don't want to cook today.
We'd like two waters, please.
Anna wants to live in Berlin.
Would you like another coffee?
We want to eat pizza this evening.
My son wants to play football.

items.why: sie (she) takes the same form as ich: sie möchte.
items.en: Lisa would like a salad.
Would you like something else to drink?
What do you want to do today?

items.why: er has no ending, like ich: er will.
items.en: He wants to buy a car.
My husband would like another beer.

answers: Ich möchte einen Tee ohne Zucker.
items.en: I'd like a tea without sugar.

listening.title: Im Restaurant
listening.intro: Julia is in a restaurant with her young son, and the waiter Stefan takes their order.

lines.speaker: Stefan
lines.de: Guten Abend! Was möchten Sie trinken?
lines.en: Good evening! What would you like to drink?

lines.speaker: Julia
lines.de: Ich möchte ein Glas Wein, bitte. Und mein Sohn möchte einen Apfelsaft.
lines.en: I'd like a glass of wine, please. And my son would like an apple juice.

lines.speaker: Stefan
lines.de: Gern. Möchten Sie auch schon bestellen?
lines.en: Certainly. Would you like to order now, too?

lines.speaker: Julia
lines.en: Yes. I'd like the vegetable soup.

lines.speaker: Julia
lines.de: Er will nur Pommes. Er will kein Gemüse essen!
lines.en: He only wants chips. He doesn't want to eat any vegetables!

lines.speaker: Stefan
lines.de: Das wollen viele Kinder. Möchte er auch ein Schnitzel?
lines.en: Lots of children want that. Would he like a schnitzel too?

lines.speaker: Julia
lines.de: Ja, gute Idee. Ein Kinderschnitzel mit Pommes, bitte.
lines.en: Yes, good idea. A children's schnitzel with chips, please.

lines.speaker: Julia
lines.de: Nein, danke. Geht es schnell? Wir haben nicht viel Zeit.
lines.en: No, thank you. Will it be quick? We don't have much time.

questions.q: What does Julia order to eat?
What doesn't her son want to eat?
Why does Julia ask if it will be quick?

speaking.en: What would you like to drink?

speaking.de: Ich möchte ein Glas Wein, bitte.
speaking.en: I'd like a glass of wine, please.
Would you like to order now, too?
He doesn't want to eat any vegetables.

writing.task: You and a friend want to go out this evening. Write 3–4 short sentences: what do you want to do, eat and drink?
writing.model: Hallo Lisa! Ich will heute Abend nicht kochen. Wollen wir Pizza essen? Ich möchte auch ein Bier trinken. Was möchtest du machen?
writing.modelEn: Hello Lisa! I don't want to cook tonight. Shall we eat pizza? I'd also like to drink a beer. What would you like to do?
